## Function Check Envelope

The range's changed files against the cards that wrote them (the envelope) and a scout session's targets (the scope).

Behaviour: readDiff(nameStatus, numstat) reads `git diff --name-status -z --no-renames` and `git diff --numstat -z --no-renames` of one range: nameStatus split on "\0" into (letter, path) pairs, an empty letter ends; A → "added", D → "deleted", any other → "modified"; numstat records "<added>\t<deleted>\t<path>" ("-" → null, a binary file); → [{path, status, added, deleted}] in nameStatus order, null counts for a path numstat lacks. MORPH_DIR = ".morph/". checkEnvelope({changed, commits: the range's Morph commits {card, model, run, paths} newest first, ownership: git's Read Ownership of the whole history, scout: {scoutId, targets, contextSlice} | null}) → {applies: commits not empty, rows, findings}. Row per changed file, in order: {path, status, added, deleted, writers: the cards (as given) of the commits whose paths hold it, distinct, commit order; owner: ownership's newest write of the path "<card> (<model or — when "">, run <run or —>)" or null; scope: null without a scout or under MORPH_DIR, else "target" | "context" | "outside" by the scout's lists}. A path under MORPH_DIR gives no finding. Per row: applies and no writer → {kind "envelope", source "primer: ownership", path, expected "written by a Morph card of the range", got "changed outside every card's targets; " + ("last Morph write <owner>" or "no Morph card ever wrote it")}; then, with a scout, scope not "target" → {kind "scope", source "scout <scoutId>", path, expected "a target of the scout session (<targets ", "-joined>)", got "changed, though the scout named it as context" | "changed, though the scout did not name it"}. Last, each scout target no changed path equals → {scope, same source, the target, expected "changed: the scout named it as a target", got "unchanged in the range"}.

Steps:
- uses: git
- reads: Ownership
- reads: Scout Record
- produces: Envelope Row

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given nameStatus "M\0a.ts\0M\0bin.dat\0D\0old.ts\0A\0src/sp ace.ts\0", numstat "2\t1\ta.ts\0-\t-\tbin.dat\0" + "0\t1\told.ts\0" + "1\t0\tsrc/sp ace.ts\0" (a real git 2.x pair); then "T\0link\0A\0new.ts\0" with "12\t0\tnew.ts\0"; then "", ""; when readDiff; then [{a.ts, modified, 2, 1}, {bin.dat, modified, null, null}, {old.ts, deleted, 0, 1}, {"src/sp ace.ts", added, 1, 0}]; [{link, modified, null, null}, {new.ts, added, 12, 0}]; []
2. given history (newest first) a-judge (m/x, run r2: tests/a.examples.test.ts), a.r1 (m/x, r2: src/a.ts), b (model "", run null: src/b.ts, src/a.ts); ownership = Read Ownership(history); commits = its first two; changed src/a.ts M +3 -1, src/b.ts M +1 -1, README.md A +2 -0, .morph/runs/r2/report.json A +40 -0, tests/a.examples.test.ts A +30 -0; scout null; when checkEnvelope; then applies true; writers ["a.r1"], [], [], [], ["a-judge"]; owners "a.r1 (m/x, run r2)", "b (—, run —)", null, null, "a-judge (m/x, run r2)"; scope null; findings envelope src/b.ts "changed outside every card's targets; last Morph write b (—, run —)", README.md "…; no Morph card ever wrote it"
3. given the same with commits []; when checkEnvelope; then applies false; every writers []; the same owners; no finding
4. given the first four changed files, commits as in 2, scout {scoutId "20261008-225320-74e423b1", targets ["src/a.ts", "src/c.ts"], contextSlice ["src/b.ts"]}; when checkEnvelope; then scopes target, context, outside, null; findings in order: envelope src/b.ts, scope src/b.ts "changed, though the scout named it as context", envelope README.md, scope README.md "changed, though the scout did not name it", scope src/c.ts "unchanged in the range", each scope expected "a target of the scout session (src/a.ts, src/c.ts)" but the last "changed: the scout named it as a target"

Data Ownership: What Read Ownership returns.
Schema:
{ commits: number, models: { model: string, commits: number }[], paths: { path: string, writes: { card: string, model: string, run: string | null }[] }[] }

Data Scout Record: .morph/scout/<id>/scout.json, read by Plan From Scout and the reviewer (P14).
Schema:
{ schema: 1, scoutId, createdAt, root, ref: string | null, question, questionSha256, protocolSha256, processor, model, seed: { source: 'primer' | 'file', path: string | null, files: string[], chars }, budgets, caps, status, answer, stopReason, spent, elapsedMs, usage, journal }

Data Envelope Row: One changed file of the range with its writers, last owner and scope.
Schema:
{ path, status: 'added' | 'modified' | 'deleted', added: number | null, deleted: number | null, writers: string[], owner: string | null, scope: 'target' | 'context' | 'outside' | null }

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

## Function Check Guardrails

The reviewer's two guardrails on the test files of a range — no test title lost, no new skipped or focused test.

Behaviour: The profile of a file is language profileForPath(path)'s id; a file without one is skipped. testTitles(text, profile): typescript (and nothing for other ids but python) — every match of /(?<![\w$.])(?:test|it)\(\s*(["'`])(.*?)\1/g, group 2 (a test.skip or it.only call is no title); python — every /^[ \t]*(?:async[ \t]+)?def[ \t]+(test\w*)[ \t]*\(/gm, group 1; in text order. skipCount(text, profile): typescript /(?<![\w$.])(?:test|it|describe)\.(?:only|skip|todo)\(/g, python /@(?:pytest\.mark\.(?:skipif|skip|xfail)|unittest\.skip)\b/g, else 0. GUARDRAILS = ["Tests Kept", "No New Skips"]. checkGuardrails({base: test files at base, head: test files at head, each {path, text}}) → {rows, findings}. Tests Kept: each base file (base order) with a profile; its distinct titles in order; a title the head file of the same path lacks (or no head file) → {kind "guardrail", source "guardrail Tests Kept", path, expected 'the test "<title>" kept', got "no test of that name at head" | "the test file is gone at head"}. No New Skips: each head file with a profile; was = skipCount of the base file of that path (0 without one), now = of the head file; now > was → {guardrail, "guardrail No New Skips", path, expected "at most <was> skipped or focused tests, as at base", got "<now> at head"}. rows = [{name "Tests Kept", files: base files with a profile, findings}, {name "No New Skips", files: head files with a profile, findings}]; findings Tests Kept's first.

Steps:
- uses: language
- produces: Guardrail Row

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given a TypeScript text with test("A: one"), it('B'), test(`C ${1}`), foo.test("no"), mytest("no2"), test.skip("D"), describe.only("E"), " test( \"F\" , …"; a Python text with def test_a, an indented async def test_b, def helper, def testing_c, @pytest.mark.skip, def test_d, @pytest.mark.skipif(…), @unittest.skip(…), @pytest.mark.xfail; when testTitles and skipCount; then with profile "go"; then ["A: one", "B", "C ${1}", "F"]; ["test_a", "test_b", "testing_c", "test_d"]; 2 and 4; 0 and [] (ref: docs/TASK_P14_reviewer.md §2.1 (the two texts, verbatim))
2. given base tests/a.test.ts (A, B, B), tests/gone.test.ts (G), README.md, tests/test_x.py (def test_one); head tests/a.test.ts (A, C), tests/test_x.py (@pytest.mark.skip over def test_one), tests/new.test.ts (it.only N, test.skip M); when checkGuardrails; then rows [{Tests Kept, 3, 2}, {No New Skips, 3, 2}]; findings: tests/a.test.ts 'the test "B" kept' "no test of that name at head"; tests/gone.test.ts "the test file is gone at head"; tests/test_x.py "at most 0 skipped or focused tests, as at base" "1 at head"; tests/new.test.ts "… 0 …" "2 at head"
3. given base and head []; then base and head the same three files with one skip each; when checkGuardrails; then rows [{Tests Kept, 0, 0}, {No New Skips, 0, 0}], no finding; then files 3 and 3, no finding

Data Guardrail Row: One guardrail's files checked and findings.
Schema:
{ name, files: number, findings: number }

## Function Find Obligations

The Functions of the record a range touches, each with the examples its tests at head must name.

Behaviour: findObligations({record, map, changed: paths changed in the range, cards: the Morph-Card values of the range's commits, titles: the test titles at head}) → {obligations, findings}. Components in record order, Functions in Component order; profile = language Resolve Profile(component.language, map.language), a failure skips the Component. unitName = the name of the first map group (map order) naming the Function, else the Function's name; unit = slugName(unitName); cut = language cutTargets(profile, component.name, unitName). codePaths = the targets of the map card whose id is unit when they are not null, else [cut code, cut test]; judgePaths = those of the map card unit + "-judge", else [cut judge]. touchedBy: first "card <id>" for each card (in the given order) whose id without a final ".r<digits>" (cardUnit) is unit or unit + "-judge", then "file <path>" for each changed path (given order) in codePaths or judgePaths; each once. Not touched → no obligation. exampleTitle(profile, name, n) = "<name> example <n>" (typescript; any profile but python) or "test_<snake name>_example_<n>" (python); hasTitle(titles, wanted, profile): a title equal to wanted or starting with wanted + ":" (python: "_"). Each example n (1-based) without a title → missing n and the finding {kind "obligation", source "record: <Component> · <Function> · example <n>", path judgePaths[0] or null, expected 'a test named "<wanted>"', got "no test title at head starts with it"}. Obligation = {component, function, unit, touchedBy, examples (the count), judge (judgePaths[0] or null), missing}; findings in obligation order.

Steps:
- uses: language
- reads: Contour Record
- reads: Contour Map
- produces: Obligation

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given tests/fixtures/reviewer/record.yaml and map.json (Load Spec); changed ["src/shop/addTax.ts", "README.md"], cards [], titles ["Add Tax example 1: the tax", "Add Tax example 3: negative", "Add Tax example 10: other"]; when findObligations; then one obligation {shop, "Add Tax", "add-tax", ["file src/shop/addTax.ts"], 3, "tests/shop/addTax.examples.test.ts", [2]}; one finding {obligation, "record: shop · Add Tax · example 2", "tests/shop/addTax.examples.test.ts", "a test named \"Add Tax example 2\"", "no test title at head starts with it"} (ref: tests/fixtures/reviewer/record.yaml (Components shop typescript, Ledger Tools python, legacy cobol), tests/fixtures/reviewer/map.json (group price-text, round-price targets))
2. given changed ["tests/shop/round.examples.test.ts"], cards ["round-price.r2", "price-text-judge", "round-price-judge"], titles ["Round Price example 1: half up", "Round Price example 2", "Format Price example 1: dollars", "Parse Price example 1: dollars", "Parse Price example 2x"]; when findObligations; then Round Price {unit "round-price", touchedBy ["card round-price", "card round-price-judge", "file tests/shop/round.examples.test.ts"], judge "tests/shop/round.examples.test.ts", missing []}; Format Price and Parse Price {unit "price-text", ["card price-text-judge"], judge "tests/shop/priceText.examples.test.ts"}, missing [] and [2]; one finding, Parse Price example 2
3. given changed ["ledger_tools/sum_rows.py"], titles ["test_sum_rows_example_1", "test_sum_rows_example_2_empty", "Sum Rows example 1: no"]; then titles ["test_sum_rows_example_12"]; when findObligations; then {"Ledger Tools", "Sum Rows", "sum-rows", ["file ledger_tools/sum_rows.py"], 2, "tests/test_sum_rows_examples.py", []}, no finding; then missing [1, 2] and two findings expecting "test_sum_rows_example_1" and "…_2"
4. given cards ["old-total", "add-tax-judge.r11"], changed ["legacy/oldTotal.ts", "tests/shop/addTax.test.ts"]; then changed [] and cards []; exampleTitle, hasTitle, cardUnit called alone; when findObligations; then legacy (cobol) skipped; Add Tax touched by ["card add-tax-judge", "file tests/shop/addTax.test.ts"]; then {[], []}; "Add Tax example 1", "test_add_tax_example_3"; hasTitle(["Add Tax example 1"], "Add Tax example 1") true, (["Add Tax example 12"], …) false; cardUnit("a.r3") "a", ("a.rx") "a.rx"

Data Contour Record: The typed record (src/contour/types.ts); every list present, every optional text null when absent, texts trimmed.
Schema:
{ version: 1, system: { name, description, requirements: string[], guardrails: string[], groups: Component[] }, actors: { name, description, uses: string[] }[], requirements: { name, description }[], guardrails: { name, description }[] }; Component = { name, description, language: string | null, requirements, guardrails, functions: { name, description, behavior, requirements, guardrails, preconditions: string[], steps: { verb: 'calls'|'reads'|'modifies'|'produces'|'uses', target }[], examples: { given, when, then, ref: string | null }[] }[], dataObjects: { name, description, schema: string | null }[], interfaces: { name, description, exposes: string[] }[] }

Data Contour Map: The typed map; snake_case keys of the document become camelCase fields, a key the map does not set is null.
Schema:
{ version: 1, package: string | null, language: string | null, docs: string[], groups: { name, functions: string[] }[], cards: ({ id } & CardFields)[], extraCards: ({ component: string | null } & CardFields)[] }; CardFields = { customId, intent: 'generate'|'patch', targets, contextSlice, dependsOn, instruction, acceptance, model, maxTokens, reasoningMaxTokens, variants }, each | null

Data Obligation: One touched Function and what its tests at head miss.
Schema:
{ component, function, unit, touchedBy: string[], examples: number, judge: string | null, missing: number[] }

## Function Plan Mutants

Single-point mutants of one code file, spread over it when they exceed the limit.

Behaviour: MUTATION_RULES, in this order (from → to; the operators with their spaces): "===" → "!==", "!==" → "===", " <= " → " < ", " >= " → " > ", " < " → " <= ", " > " → " >= ", " + " → " - ", " - " → " + ", "&&" → "||", "||" → "&&", "true" → "false" and "false" → "true" (these two as whole words: no [A-Za-z0-9_$] on either side). quotedMask(line) → one boolean per char, true inside a "…", '…' or `…` string (the quotes included, a backslash escapes the next char). planMutants(path, text, limit) → Mutant[]: lines = text split on "\n"; a line whose start matches /^\s*(?:\/\/|\/\*|\*|#|import\b|export\s+(?:type\s+)?\{)/ is skipped; on the others the code ends at the first "//" outside a string. Every occurrence of every rule wholly before that end and starting outside a string is a mutant, sorted by the occurrence's index, then rule order; mutant {path, line (1-based), column (1-based, of the operator's first non-space char), rule "<from trimmed> → <to trimmed>", text: the whole text with that one occurrence replaced}. Lines in order. limit ≤ 0 → []; total ≤ limit → all; else the mutants at indices floor(i × total / limit) for i = 0 … limit − 1.

Steps:
- produces: Mutant

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given src/f.ts = an import line, a comment "// a < b in a comment", "export function f(a: number, b: number): boolean {", " if (a === b && a > 0) return true;", ' return a + b >= 10 || s === "a < b"; // b - a', "}" and a final newline; limit 50; when planMutants; then 8 mutants [line, column, rule]: [4, 9, "=== → !=="], [4, 15, "&& → ||"], [4, 20, "> → >="], [4, 32, "true → false"], [5, 12, "+ → -"], [5, 16, ">= → >"], [5, 22, "|| → &&"], [5, 27, "=== → !=="]; the first text has "a !== b" and is otherwise the source (ref: docs/TASK_P14_reviewer.md §2.1 (the text verbatim))
2. given the same with limit 3, 0 and 9; when planMutants; then the mutants 0, 2, 5: [4, 9], [4, 20], [5, 16]; []; all 8
3. given quotedMask of say("a\"b", 'c') + 1 (20 chars); src/t.ts "const truey = trueish && untrue;\nconst t = true;\nconst u = !false;\n", limit 10; when quotedMask; planMutants; then "00001111110011100000"; [1, 23, "&& → ||"], [2, 11, "true → false"], [3, 12, "false → true"]

Data Mutant: One single-point mutant of a code file.
Schema:
{ path, line, column, rule, text }

env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

## Function Render Findings

The review document — numbered findings with EXPECTED/GOT and a source tag, the counts, the verdict and a markdown page.

Behaviour: KIND_ORDER = ["obligation", "envelope", "scope", "guardrail", "mutation"]. orderFindings(findings): stable sort by the kind's index (a kind not in KIND_ORDER after them all), then numbered {id "F<n>" from 1, kind, source, path, expected, got}. renderFindings({base, head, changed: {path, status, added, deleted, writers, scope}[], obligations: {component, function, touchedBy, examples, missing}[], guardrails: {name, files, findings}[], mutants: {path, line, rule, killed}[] | null, findings}) → {range "<base>..<head>", verdict "clean" when no finding else "findings", counts {files, obligations, examples (sum), missing (sum of lengths), mutants (count or null), killed (count or null), findings, byKind: the five kinds at 0 then the counts, an unknown kind added after them}, findings (ordered), markdown}. markdown = these lines "\n"-joined: "# Review <range>", "", "Clean: no findings." or "<n> findings: <kind> <count>, … (byKind order)."; "", "## Changed files (<n>)", "", "| file | status | lines | written by | scope |", "|---|---|---|---|---|", a row per file "| <path> | <status> | +<added> -<deleted> (binary when either is null) | <writers ", "> or — | <scope or —> |"; "", "## Obligations (<n> Functions, <e> examples, <m> missing)", "", and when any: "| Function | touched by | examples | missing |", "|---|---|---|---|", "| <component> · <function> | <touchedBy ", "> | <examples> | <missing ", "> or — |", ""; "## Guardrails", "", "| guardrail | files | findings |", "|---|---|---|", a row each, ""; with mutants: "## Mutants (<killed> of <n> killed)", "", and when any "| at | rule | result |", "|---|---|---|", "| <path>:<line> | <rule> | killed or survived |", ""; "## Findings", "", ("None.", "" when none); per finding "### <id> · <kind> · <source>", "", "- path: <path or —>", "- EXPECTED: <expected>", "- GOT: <got>", "". Every "|" inside a table cell is written "\|".

- produces: Review
